title: Qman DirectPath authoritative host-snapshot publication trace
description: Closed evidence for one OP-CAPTURE-HOST-SNAPSHOT execution. It retains the actual canonical capture batch and provider outputs, separately identifies captured candidate and persisted-after DeviceRecord V3 sets, binds the current capability and freshness policy bytes plus both policy authorities, the signed HostSnapshot, exact HostAuthority and global AvailabilityAuthority before/after states, raw operation exchange, one four-authority repository transaction, predecessor/preflight/prepared/final rollback-authority artifacts, and a zero-partial-writes witness. A schema name, digest, SQL log, fake provider, or component fixture without these actual bytes is not product publication proof.

canonicalBytesBase64.x-qmanCanonicalBytesRule: Decode with strict RFC 4648 base64. The decoded value is non-empty exact CANONICAL-JSON-V1 UTF-8 bytes with no duplicate keys, noncanonical spelling, floating-point value, or trailing byte.

providerCaptureOutputEnvelope.x-qmanPortableReplayProfile: This fixed portable envelope is the executable component boundary for retained provider output. A target provider adapter emits one exact row per covered device. PCI rows retain the raw conventional 256-byte configuration capture or a closed failure; generic facts remain decoder premises until a target-commit decoder/build receipt proves their origin.

providerCaptureSemanticFactsEnvelope.x-qmanPortableReplayProfile: The normalized envelope must independently reproduce the exact provider fact rows and, for PCI captures, the exact structure and FLR facts re-derived from providerCaptureOutputEnvelope raw bytes. It is component evidence only until the target decoder/build binding is externally attested.

captureClosureVerifierAlgorithmIdentity.x-qmanIdentityRule: algorithmIdentityDigest is SHA-256 over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-CAPTURE-CLOSURE-VERIFIER-ALGORITHM/V2) || 0x00 || CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of this complete object with only algorithmIdentityDigest set to null. The five ordered schema bindings close the exact transitive schemas consumed by the component verifier. This identity is not a binary hash, target build attestation or product release identity.

captureClosureVerificationReceipt.x-qmanAuthorityBoundary: This receipt proves exact retained component inputs and deterministic replay only. candidateSnapshotEpoch/candidateResourceVersion are caller-stamped coordinates whose internal committed-row shape is verified but whose next-version authority still requires repository CAS. freshnessTimeBasis is caller capture completion, not trusted transaction time. productAuthorized is permanently false; the enumerated target/repository/authority evidence cannot be supplied by self-declared receipt fields.

deviceFactBinding.x-qmanReplayAndEqualityRule: Decode this providerCapture canonicalOutputBase64 and semanticFactsBase64 under their retained fixed schemas and replay the conventional PCI configuration parser. The unique decoded row selected by [deviceUid,currentBdf] exact-equals this closed binding. providerFact.factId exact-equals pciStructureFact.providerFactId; providerFact.evidenceHash exact-equals pciStructureFact.captureEvidenceDigest; pciFlrCapabilityFact.structureFactDigest exact-equals pciStructureFact.structureFactDigest. The decoded raw 256-byte configuration exact-equals pciStructureFact.rawConfigSpaceHexOrNull when captureStatus=COMPLETE and independently re-derives every identity, raw header byte, headerLayout, multifunction flag, subordinate-bus fact, PCIe capability field, structureFactDigest, FLR state, Device Capabilities dword, functionLevelResetCapableOrNull and flrFactDigest. UNAVAILABLE exact-replays the closed UNKNOWN/null shape and retained failure disposition; no caller-supplied normalized fact may replace this replay.

providerCapture.x-qmanDeviceFactBindingRule: coveredDeviceUids is non-empty and exact-equals the sorted candidate DeviceRecord deviceUid set whose retained provenance contains this provider identity/version/definition; a zero-coverage provider rejects the batch instead of disappearing from providerFactsDigest. deviceFactBindings is the PCI-configuration-specific subset and may be empty for a non-PCI provider. Every PCI binding is owned by this capture: its deviceUid is in coveredDeviceUids; its providerFact providerId/providerVersion/providerDefinitionDigest exact-equal this providerCapture identity triple, its observedAt lies inclusively within [captureStartedAt,captureCompletedAt], and its evidenceHash is reachable from the exact decoded provider output rather than an independently supplied label. For one provider capture, [deviceUid,currentBdf], providerFact.factId, pciStructureFact.structureFactDigest and pciFlrCapabilityFact.flrFactDigest are each unique.

deviceRecordArtifactSet.x-qmanCanonicalOrder: ascending CANONICAL-JSON-V1 bytes of recordBinding.deviceUid; duplicate deviceUid values are invalid

x-qmanHashRules: Every envelopeSha256, payloadBytesSha256, canonicalBytesSha256 and instanceBytesSha256 is lowercase sha256:hex of the strict-base64-decoded exact bytes in that wrapper. Every wrapper carrying state or instance must decode to byte-equal CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of that complete object. requestEnvelope.payloadHash equals requestPayload.payloadBytesSha256; resultEnvelope.payloadHash equals resultPayload.payloadBytesSha256; each envelope/payload schemaRef and schema digest pair exact-equals the other and the portable normative-source digest for directpath-operation-payload.schema.json.

For each providerCapture, outputBytesSha256 is SHA-256 of the decoded canonicalOutputBase64 bytes. semanticFactsDigest is SHA-256 over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/PROVIDER-SEMANTIC-FACTS/V1), one zero byte, and the decoded semanticFactsBase64 bytes; provider output and semantic facts both validate against their retained fixed schema/version. Raw output bytes are evidence but are deliberately not the no-change comparator.

deviceSemanticProjection is the unique V2 machine-readable projection declared by x-qmanProjectionFromDeviceRecord: copy every listed DeviceRecord V3 field byte-for-byte, normalize health only by omitting observedAt, normalize provenance only by omitting captureStartedAt, capturedAt and providerFacts[].observedAt, replace subjectType/schemaVersion with the declared literals, and omit generations/deviceRecordHash. For the digest preimage, deep-copy that stored projection, set deviceSemanticDigest and every exact wildcard-expanded digestNullPaths entry to null, retain every other key/value, and hash ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/DEVICE-TOPOLOGY-SEMANTIC-PROJECTION/V2), one zero byte, and CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of that closed intermediate object. Identity, BDF, normalized headerLayout, multifunction, subordinate-bus presence/value, PCIe capability state/version/device-port type, function-level-reset state/capability, role/function value, IOMMU mode/backend/provider identity and complete BDF membership, resolved physical-isolation UIDs, dependency kinds/states/edges/actions, reset behavior/affected set, owner behavior/groups, BAR values, interrupt values, health state/result/reason and traits are semantic. Raw configuration bytes/SHA, raw header byte, capability offsets/registers, provider fact IDs, failure evidence, component authority metadata and evidence/provenance/self-digests remain retained evidence but are set to null only in the comparator preimage. The intermediate null-bearing object need not validate as a stored projection.

topologyDigest follows the V2 topologyProjection.x-qmanDigestProjection exactly: construct {subjectType,schemaVersion,hostId,kernelBootId,hostEpoch,agentGeneration,members,topologyDigest}, replace each sorted member by exactly {deviceUid,deviceSemanticDigest}, set topologyDigest to null, and hash ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-TOPOLOGY-PROJECTION/V2), one zero byte, and CANONICAL-JSON-V1. providerFactsDigest remains V1 and uses ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-PROVIDER-PROJECTION/V1), one zero byte, and the complete providerSemanticProjection with only providerFactsDigest set to null; each provider entry contains only stable provider identity/version/definition and coveredDeviceUids, the exact sorted set of candidate DeviceRecord deviceUid values whose retained provenance contains at least one matching provider fact.

noChangeProjectionHash follows noChangeProjection.x-qmanDigestProjection: hash ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-NO-CHANGE/V2), one zero byte, and CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of the complete V2 noChangeProjection with only noChangeProjectionHash set to null. Timestamps, barriers, raw output, semanticFactsDigest, evidence/provenance digests, repository versions, snapshot/device generations, signatures and content hashes are retained elsewhere but cannot enter this closed comparator. A behavioral PCI structure/FLR field, provider identity/version/definition, provider-to-device coverage, topology membership or policy change does enter it.

capabilityPolicy.state.policyHash follows directpath-capability-policy.schema.json exactly: deep-copy the complete policy, set only policyHash to null, and SHA-256 the CANONICAL-JSON-V1 bytes. freshnessPolicy.state.policyHash is SHA-256 over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-FRESHNESS-POLICY/V1), one zero byte, and CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of the complete freshnessPolicy state with only policyHash set to null. freshnessDecision.decisionDigest uses ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-FRESHNESS-DECISION/V1), one zero byte, and the complete decision including evaluationDisposition with only decisionDigest set to null. captureBatchDigest uses ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-CAPTURE-BATCH/V1), one zero byte, and the complete captureBatch with only captureBatchDigest set to null.

deviceRecordSetDigest is a function of one selected snapshotOrNull: use SHA-256 over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-DEVICE-RECORD-SET/V1), one zero byte, and CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of exactly {hostSnapshotContentHashOrNull:null,deviceRecordDigests:[]} when selected snapshotOrNull is null; otherwise use exactly {hostSnapshotContentHashOrNull:selectedSnapshot.state.contentHash,deviceRecordDigests:selectedSnapshot.state.deviceRecordDigests}. The commit record always selects hostSnapshotAfter; each BEFORE/AFTER visibility probe independently selects its corresponding observed snapshot state. It is never inferred from predecessor existence, row count or a caller label.

repositoryTransaction.expectationHash and snapshotPublicationCasResult.expectationHashOrNull use snapshotPublicationCasExpectation.x-qmanDigestProjection: SHA-256 over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-PUBLICATION-CAS-EXPECTATION/V1), one zero byte, and the exact closed four-authority expectation with only expectationHash set to null. repositoryTransaction.resolvedAuthorityVectorHash and snapshotPublicationCasResult.committedAuthorityHashOrNull use snapshotPublicationResolvedAuthorityVector.x-qmanDigestProjection under ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-PUBLICATION-AUTHORITY-STATE/V1): COMMITTED selects after HostAuthority/AvailabilityAuthority artifact hashes, NO_CHANGE selects their byte-identical before hashes, and both select the unchanged capability/freshness policy authority artifact hashes. Both hashes are non-null for COMMITTED and NO_CHANGE.

snapshotRollbackAuthority.rollbackAuthorityPreflight replays directpath-host-snapshot-rollback-anchor.schema.json#/$defs/rollbackAuthorityPreflightReceipt exactly, including its domain-separated receipt digest and root quorum signatures. For a committed path, preparedOrNull.state.prepareReceipt.rollbackAuthorityPreflightReceiptDigest exact-equals that preflight state.receiptDigest.

For FULL_CANONICAL_INSTANCE, beforeDigestOrNull/afterDigestOrNull is SHA-256 of the exact retained before/after row CANONICAL-JSON-V1 bytes. For AVAILABILITY_AUTHORITY_LAST_MUTATION_DIGEST_NULL, deep-copy the exact before or after AvailabilityAuthority row and set only lastMutationDigest to null. For PUBLICATION_AUDIT_MUTATION_SET_AND_AUDIT_DIGEST_NULL, set only mutationSetHash and auditDigest to null. For PUBLICATION_OUTBOX_MUTATION_SET_AND_OUTBOX_DIGEST_NULL, set only mutationSetHash and outboxDigest to null. For PUBLICATION_COMMIT_DERIVED_FIELDS_NULL, deep-copy the exact repositoryCommitRecord and set exactly mutationSetHash, availabilityAuthorityAfterInstanceSha256, auditRecordInstanceSha256, outboxRecordInstanceSha256 and commitRecordDigest to null while retaining anchorReservationId, anchorPrepareReceiptDigest, anchorCandidateProjectionDigest, HostSnapshot/DeviceRecord/HostAuthority digests and every other field. The corresponding beforeDigestOrNull/afterDigestOrNull is SHA-256 of CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of that exact projection without a domain prefix; intermediate null-bearing objects need not validate as stored rows. INSERT beforeDigestOrNull is null and UPDATE applies the same declared projection to the predecessor.

mutationSetHashOrNull is then SHA-256 over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-MUTATION-SET/V1), one zero byte, and CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of the exact canonical mutation array. Only after this hash exists is it copied into AvailabilityAuthority.lastMutationDigest, publicationAuditRecord.mutationSetHash and publicationOutboxRecord.mutationSetHash; those stored values never feed back into their mutation afterDigest projections.

publicationOutboxRecord.payloadHash is SHA-256 over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-PUBLISHED-PAYLOAD/V1), one zero byte, and CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of exactly {eventType,aggregateId,anchorReservationId,anchorPrepareReceiptDigest,anchorCandidateProjectionDigest,requiredAnchorVersion,deliveryGate,snapshotContentHash,hostAuthorityResourceVersion,availabilityAuthorityResourceVersion}. auditDigest is SHA-256 over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-PUBLICATION-AUDIT/V1), one zero byte, and the complete audit record with only auditDigest set to null. outboxDigest analogously uses ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-PUBLICATION-OUTBOX/V1) with only outboxDigest set to null. Both self-digests retain the already-computed non-null mutationSetHash, and each actual wrapper then hashes the complete stored row including its self-digest.

publicationAuditRecord.auditEventId is the literal prefix audit: followed by the 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters of SHA-256 over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-PUBLICATION-AUDIT-EVENT-ID/V1), one zero byte, and CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of exactly {operationId,commandId,requestHash,operationRequestContextDigest,decisionContextDigest,expectationHash,repositoryId,transactionId,commitId,aggregateId,createdAt,commitClockBefore,commitClockAfter,anchorReservationId,anchorPrepareReceiptDigest,anchorCandidateProjectionDigest}. publicationOutboxRecord.outboxEventId uses the byte-identical subject and the literal prefix outbox: under ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-PUBLICATION-OUTBOX-EVENT-ID/V1), one zero byte. The subject contains only verified request/decision, repository commit-time and PREPARED rollback-authority facts; mutationSetHash, row self-digests, row artifact hashes, resolvedAuthorityVectorHash, complete rollback/mutation/result context digests and traceDigest are excluded.

repositoryCommitRecord.commitRecordDigest is SHA-256 over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-REPOSITORY-COMMIT/V1), one zero byte, and CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of the complete commit record with only commitRecordDigest set to null. Its six instance/set digests exact-equal the retained after HostSnapshot, DeviceRecord set, HostAuthority, AvailabilityAuthority, audit and outbox artifacts; its reservation/preparation/candidate fields exact-equal snapshotRollbackAuthority.preparedOrNull. commitWitness.commitRecordDigestOrNull exact-equals state.commitRecordDigest; the wrapper instanceBytesSha256 separately hashes the complete stored commit row including that digest.

visibilityProbe.probeDigest is SHA-256 over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-VISIBILITY-PROBE/V1), one zero byte, and CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of the complete probe with only probeDigest set to null. For outboxDeliveryWitness, deep-copy the complete witness, set deliveryReceiptDigest and dispatcherSignature to null, and hash ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-OUTBOX-DELIVERY/V1), one zero byte, and CANONICAL-JSON-V1; then verify dispatcherSignature over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-OUTBOX-DELIVERY-SIGNATURE/V1), one zero byte, and CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of exactly {dispatcherKeyId,deliveredAt,deliveryReceiptDigest} using the retained trustContext key ring and CONTROL_REPOSITORY_EVIDENCE role. Intermediate null fields need not validate. Each wrapper hashes the complete instance including self-digest/signature. traceDigest is computed last over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-PUBLICATION-TRACE/V1), one zero byte, and CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of the complete trace with only traceDigest set to null; no CaseCompletionRecord or ExecutionEvidenceIndex digest enters this preimage.
x-qmanCaptureClosureRules: The component-only HOST_SNAPSHOT_CAPTURE_CLOSURE_VERIFIER_V2 receipt binds one ordered algorithm identity containing exactly five transitive schema bindings [capability-policy, publication-trace, identity-v1, portable-entities, portable-hash-subjects] and exactly ten validation stages; every schema digest is recomputed from the exact ContractSchemas bytes, and an independently verified capability policy is replayed only when its capability-policy schema digest exact-equals that identity. Shape/count, encoded/decoded byte, JSON node/depth, retained provider-fact and dependency-edge limits are enforced before expensive schema walks, uniqueness is canonical-hash indexed, mandatory freshness lookup is indexed by [providerId,factId], and dependency reciprocity is precomputed rather than repeatedly scanning the record set. Candidate records prove only internal coordinate composability: every deviceGeneration equals the shared candidateSnapshotEpoch and every record shares candidateResourceVersion. Both coordinates remain caller-stamped and require the product repository's SERIALIZABLE CAS against HostAuthority; freshness is evaluated only against caller-supplied captureCompletedAt, not trusted transaction time, so TRUSTED_PUBLICATION_EVALUATION_TIME_REQUIRED remains one of eight fixed blockers and productAuthorized remains false.

Every provider capture shares one collectionBarrierId, hostId, kernelBootId, hostEpoch and agentGeneration; captureStartedAt <= provider start <= provider completion <= captureCompletedAt. Provider IDs are unique under [providerId,providerVersion,providerDefinitionDigest]. Unknown, missing, contradictory, cross-boot or cross-barrier mandatory facts reject publication rather than become permissive defaults.

captureBatch.instance is the actual closed capture batch and canonicalCaptureBatchBase64 is its exact canonical encoding. Each provider retains actual output and normalized semantic-facts bytes. The portable component replay profile uses #/$defs/providerCaptureOutputEnvelope and #/$defs/providerCaptureSemanticFactsEnvelope: the former retains the conventional raw 256-byte PCI configuration capture or closed failure per PCI row, and the latter independently retains normalized PCI structure/FLR facts; both retain exact provider facts and capture coordinates. Target-specific generic-provider raw acquisition/decoding still requires a decoder/build binding for every outputSchemaRef and semanticFactsSchemaRef resolved at targetRepositoryCommit in the same execution evidence; a schema label, normalized generic fact, or digest alone has zero product capture coverage.

Each providerCapture.coveredDeviceUids exact-equals the non-empty sorted candidate DeviceRecord deviceUid set whose retained provenance contains that capture's provider identity/version/definition. Generic non-PCI providers may have an empty deviceFactBindings array but cannot have zero coverage. Across the union of the PCI-specific captureBatch.instance.providerCaptures[].deviceFactBindings there is an exact bijection with candidateDeviceRecords: every candidate DeviceRecord V3 has exactly one binding selected by [deviceUid,currentBdf], and no binding lacks a candidate record. Each candidate DeviceRecord provenance.captureStartedAt/capturedAt exact-equals the enclosing captureBatch captureStartedAt/captureCompletedAt; every retained provider observedAt lies in that interval. The binding providerFact exact-equals the unique candidate DeviceRecord provenance.providerFacts row selected by role.pciStructureFact.providerFactId and also exact-binds its containing providerCapture identity/version/definition, coveredDeviceUids and capture interval. binding.pciStructureFact byte-equals candidate DeviceRecord.role.pciStructureFact and binding.pciFlrCapabilityFact byte-equals candidate DeviceRecord.resetContract.pciFlrCapabilityFact. The retained raw provider bytes and semantic-facts bytes independently replay that binding, including UID/BDF association, identity, raw header, normalized layout, multifunction, PCIe port type and FLR capability; any duplicate, omission, cross-provider substitution, digest-only label or mismatch rejects publication.

candidateDeviceRecords is the complete FULL_HOST DeviceRecord V3 artifact set produced by this capture and is the only set consumed by capture/provider/provenance/semantic reconstruction. deviceRecords is the complete persisted-after set selected by the publication decision. currentDeviceRecordsOrNull is null only when no current snapshot exists and otherwise is the complete persisted predecessor set for hostSnapshotBeforeOrNull. Every decoded record validates against its fixed schemaRef and deviceRecordHash recomputes under the portable entity rule. Candidate records all carry the proposed HostAuthority-before plus-one snapshotEpoch/resourceVersion coordinates even when NO_CHANGE later performs no write. For every committed decision, deviceRecords byte-equals candidateDeviceRecords and each HostSnapshotAfter.deviceRecordDigests exact-equals that set. For NO_CHANGE, deviceRecords byte-equals currentDeviceRecordsOrNull and hostSnapshotAfter byte-equals hostSnapshotBeforeOrNull; newly captured candidate provenance/timestamps never masquerade as persisted rows. This full-publication V1 composition is bounded to 4096 candidate/current/persisted records even though the standalone capture component supports a larger candidate batch.

The V2 topologyProjection is independently reconstructed from the decoded complete candidateDeviceRecords set using the machine-readable exact-copy/normalization and digest-null projections. The KNOWN IOMMU domain target UID set exact-equals iommuProvider.kernelIommuGroup after resolving every current BDF against the same complete set; dependency domains/actions, physical-isolation membership, reset/owner groups, PCI structure/FLR facts, BAR/interrupt/health/trait fields and every retained provenance/evidence artifact satisfy DeviceRecord V3 before only the declared raw/evidence/digest/provenance paths are nulled for the semantic comparator. headerLayout, multifunctionOrNull, pcieCapabilityState, pcieCapabilityVersionOrNull, pcieDevicePortTypeOrNull, pciFlrCapabilityFact.state and functionLevelResetCapableOrNull remain semantic and must never be nulled. providerSemanticProjection.providers exact-equals the providerCapture identity/version/definition set; each providerCapture.coveredDeviceUids and matching projection coveredDeviceUids both exact-equal the sorted candidate DeviceRecord deviceUid set whose retained provenance.providerFacts contains that provider identity. semanticFactsSchemaRef, semanticFactsDigest, raw bytes, observedAt, evidenceHash and caller-supplied fact labels never enter providerFactsDigest. candidateNoChangeProjection byte-equals captureBatch.instance.noChangeProjection and binds the independently reconstructed topology/provider digests, policyHash=capabilityPolicy.state.policyHash, and snapshotFreshnessPolicyHash=freshnessPolicy.state.policyHash.

The five trustContext wrappers retain and validate the actual trust-root set, key ring, key-ring history, trust rollback anchor and live trust-anchor freshness bytes. configuredTrustRootDigest and hostSnapshotSignerKeyId resolve through those exact artifacts, their external rollback/freshness checks pass, and the HostSnapshot signature/contentHash is replayed from the exact retained bytes. OUT_OF_BAND_CONFIG is a source constraint, not a self-declared trust label.

The decoded request/result payload bytes validate under the fixed OP-CAPTURE profiles and exact normative-source SHA. Their enclosing raw envelopes validate under the fixed request/result envelope fragments; commandId, operationId, payloadHash/schema fields, portableContractSha256, targetRepositoryObjectFormat and raw targetRepositoryCommit exact-equal this trace. A SHA1 target is exactly 40 lowercase hex and SHA256 exactly 64 lowercase hex. Request currentHostAuthority, currentAvailabilityAuthority, capabilityPolicy, capabilityPolicyAuthority, snapshotFreshnessPolicy and snapshotFreshnessPolicyAuthority exact-project the six retained actual wrapper IDs, versions, schema refs and instanceBytesSha256 under the payload rule. hostSnapshotRollbackAnchorOrNull and hostSnapshotAnchorFreshnessOrNull exact-project snapshotRollbackAuthority.beforeOrNull and beforeFreshnessOrNull, never the post-decision artifacts; genesis carries both null. The request cannot carry open policy fields, thresholds or mandatory-selector values.

A successful resultEnvelope carries the resolved post-decision authority rather than echoing the request CAS vector: controllerGeneration and hostEpochs remain request-equal, snapshotEpoch selects hostSnapshotAfter, resourceVersions is the sorted closed four-authority set selecting committed HostAuthority/AvailabilityAuthority versions for COMMITTED and byte-identical current versions for NO_CHANGE, and both policy authority versions remain current. policyHash selects capabilityPolicy.state.policyHash, profileHash is null and authoritativeStates is empty. COMMITTED committedResourceVersions is exactly the HostAuthority/AvailabilityAuthority before-to-after pair and receiptHashes is exactly the retained rollback preflight, prepare, finalized anchor receipt, after-freshness state and durable repository commit record; NO_CHANGE committedResourceVersions is empty and receiptHashes is exactly preflight, finalized anchor receipt and after-freshness state. Each receiptSha256 hashes those exact canonical receipt/state bytes, never result, context or trace bytes, so no result hash enters the repository commit DAG.

For a successful result, body.outputOrNull.hostSnapshot is exactly {documentKind=HOST_SNAPSHOT,documentId=hostSnapshotAfter.state.contentHash,documentVersion=hostSnapshotAfter.state.snapshotEpoch,canonicalProfile=CANONICAL-JSON-V1,schemaRef=contracts/directpath-portable-hash-subjects.schema.json#/$defs/hostSnapshot,contentHash=hostSnapshotAfter.instanceBytesSha256}; snapshotContentHash equals hostSnapshotAfter.state.contentHash. inventorySignature uses documentKind=HOST_INVENTORY_SIGNATURE, documentId=the same contentHash, documentVersion=hostSnapshotAfter.state.keyRingVersion, the same HostSnapshot schemaRef and contentHash=hostSnapshotAfter.instanceBytesSha256. advancedHostAuthority is exactly {entityType=ENTITY-HOST-AUTHORITY,entityId=hostAuthorityAfter.state.hostId,resourceVersion=hostAuthorityAfter.state.resourceVersion,generationOrNull=hostAuthorityAfter.state.agentGeneration,contentHash=hostAuthorityAfter.instanceBytesSha256}; factProvenanceSetHash equals captureBatch.instance.providerSemanticProjection.providerFactsDigest.

The same result output projects snapshotRollbackAnchor exactly as {documentKind=HOST_SNAPSHOT_ROLLBACK_ANCHOR,documentId=snapshotRollbackAuthority.after.state.anchorDigest,documentVersion=snapshotRollbackAuthority.after.state.anchorVersion,canonicalProfile=CANONICAL-JSON-V1,schemaRef=contracts/directpath-host-snapshot-rollback-anchor.schema.json,contentHash=snapshotRollbackAuthority.after.instanceBytesSha256} and snapshotAnchorFreshness exactly as {documentKind=ANCHOR_FRESHNESS_ENVELOPE,documentId=snapshotRollbackAuthority.afterFreshness.state.envelopeId,documentVersion=snapshotRollbackAuthority.afterFreshness.state.resourceVersion,canonicalProfile=CANONICAL-JSON-V1,schemaRef=contracts/directpath-anchor-freshness-envelope.schema.json,contentHash=snapshotRollbackAuthority.afterFreshness.instanceBytesSha256}. The specialized snapshotPublicationCasResult decision is COMMITTED for a committed publication and NO_CHANGE otherwise; its capability/freshness policy expectations, repositoryTransaction.expectationHash, resolvedAuthorityVectorHash, committed versions, mutationSetHashOrNull, commitRecordDigestOrNull and publicationMutationCount exact-project this trace. It contains no generic casMutation array: COMMITTED publicationMutationCount equals deviceRecords length plus six for HostSnapshot, HostAuthority, AvailabilityAuthority, publication audit, gated outbox and durable commit-record rows; NO_CHANGE is zero while retaining both authority-vector hashes.
x-qmanPublicationRules: The verified OP-CAPTURE-HOST-SNAPSHOT request is replayed from its exact canonical request-envelope and detached request-payload bytes before publication. repositoryTransaction.operationId is OP-CAPTURE-HOST-SNAPSHOT; commandId, requestHash and operationRequestContextDigest exact-equal that verified request; decisionContextDigest and expectationHash exact-equal the replayed publication decision. repositoryCommitRecord exact-equals repositoryTransaction on operationId, commandId, requestHash, operationRequestContextDigest, decisionContextDigest, expectationHash, repositoryId, transactionId, commitClockBefore and commitClockAfter. The request payload and envelope additionally exact-bind the retained publication read set, authority vector, issuedAt/deadlineAt, target repository object format/commit and payload/request hashes under the fixed operation-request verifier; a caller scalar, structurally valid substitute request or same-command different-requestHash request is not an authority.

repositoryTransaction expected HostAuthority, AvailabilityAuthority, capability-policy authority and freshness-policy authority resource versions exact-equal the four retained current authority states; expectedCapabilityPolicyHash and expectedFreshnessPolicyHash exact-equal the two retained policy state hashes. The SERIALIZABLE transaction reads/locks and compares all four current rows at one snapshot before any decision or insert/update becomes visible; either policy switch races to conflict rather than deciding with stale policy bytes. expectationHash and resolvedAuthorityVectorHash recompute from the closed four-authority hash subjects and exact-project the specialized result for both COMMITTED and NO_CHANGE.

For GENESIS_COMMITTED or INCARNATION_GENESIS_COMMITTED, HostAuthority before is exactly the durable unpublished-incarnation form [lastSnapshotEpoch=0,currentSnapshotContentHash=null,RECONCILING]. HostSnapshot after has snapshotEpoch=1 and previousSnapshotContentHashOrNull=null. GENESIS has no earlier host rollback anchor; INCARNATION_GENESIS has an earlier committed anchor from an older host/agent incarnation.

For every committed publication, hostAuthorityBefore and hostAuthorityAfter exact-equal on hostId,hostEpoch,kernelBootId,agentIdentity,agentGeneration and cooperationState. The capture publisher owns only lastSnapshotEpoch,currentSnapshotContentHash,lastObservedAt and resourceVersion; it cannot change owner/backend/lease/journal reconciliation state or promote RECONCILING to ONLINE_COOPERATIVE. Genesis therefore remains RECONCILING after publication; a separate reconciler authority may later advance cooperationState.

For every committed publication, hostSnapshotAfter.snapshotEpoch=hostAuthorityBefore.lastSnapshotEpoch+1, hostAuthorityAfter.resourceVersion=hostAuthorityBefore.resourceVersion+1, lastSnapshotEpoch equals that new signed epoch, currentSnapshotContentHash equals the new contentHash, and HostSnapshot.hostAuthorityResourceVersion equals the committed after resourceVersion. hostSnapshotAfter.capturedAt and hostAuthorityAfter.lastObservedAt both exact-equal captureBatch.instance.captureCompletedAt. No other HostAuthority field changes.

SUCCESSOR_COMMITTED requires currentNoChangeProjectionOrNull.noChangeProjectionHash != candidateNoChangeProjection.noChangeProjectionHash and previousSnapshotContentHashOrNull equals the exact predecessor contentHash. REFRESH_COMMITTED requires the two complete no-change projections byte-equal, evaluationDisposition=CURRENT_POLICY_MATCHED and refreshRequired=true, yet still publishes a new immutable epoch under the same predecessor/CAS rules. NO_CHANGE requires those complete projections byte-equal, evaluationDisposition=CURRENT_POLICY_MATCHED and refreshRequired=false. GENESIS/INCARNATION use GENESIS_NO_CURRENT. A freshness-policy hash change selects SUCCESSOR with ACTIVE_POLICY_CHANGED_FORCES_SUCCESSOR, oldestMandatoryEvidenceObservedAtOrNull=null and refreshRequired=false; candidate capture closure, not predecessor records, proves the newly mandatory selectors. No other decision/projection/disposition combination is valid.

capabilityPolicy.state policyId/policyVersion/policyHash exact-match capabilityPolicyAuthority.state policyId/policyVersion/policyDigest, and capabilityPolicyAuthority.resourceVersion exact-matches repository expectation and request authority ref. freshnessPolicy.state.policyHash recomputes by the fixed hash rule. freshnessPolicyAuthority.state policyId/policyVersion/policyDigest exact-equal freshnessPolicy.state policyId/policyVersion/policyHash, and freshnessDecision policyId/policyVersion/policyDigest/policyAuthorityResourceVersion plus both maximum ages exact-equal those actual policy/authority fields. candidateNoChangeProjection.policyHash and hostSnapshotAfter.state.policyHash equal capabilityPolicy.state.policyHash; candidateNoChangeProjection.snapshotFreshnessPolicyHash and hostSnapshotAfter.state.snapshotFreshnessPolicyHash equal freshnessPolicy.state.policyHash. Current projection/HostSnapshot bind their own predecessor policy hashes. A change to either policy necessarily changes the comparator and selects SUCCESSOR_COMMITTED.

freshnessDecision.evaluatedAt exact-equals repositoryTransaction.beganAt, the trusted SERIALIZABLE read/linearization time, not a caller clock; capabilityPolicy.state must still satisfy effectiveAt <= evaluatedAt < expiresAt, with equality at expiresAt rejected even if capture completed earlier. Convert TIMESTAMP-UTC-US-V1 to integer Unix microseconds and reject a non-null basis later than evaluatedAt. For GENESIS_NO_CURRENT, both current timestamps are null and refreshRequired=false. For ACTIVE_POLICY_CHANGED_FORCES_SUCCESSOR, currentSnapshotCapturedAtOrNull exact-equals hostSnapshotBeforeOrNull.state.capturedAt, oldestMandatoryEvidenceObservedAtOrNull is null and refreshRequired=false; the active policy is never applied partially to predecessor records. Only for CURRENT_POLICY_MATCHED, collect all exact matching providerFacts observedAt values from currentDeviceRecordsOrNull for every [providerId,factId] selector; every selector must match at least one retained fact, oldestMandatoryEvidenceObservedAtOrNull is their minimum, and refreshRequired is exactly whether snapshot age or oldest mandatory evidence age is greater than or equal to its threshold. Equality at the threshold requires refresh.

Every committed publication increments AvailabilityAuthority.resourceVersion by exactly one in the same transaction. Its lastMutationDigest equals commitWitness.mutationSetHashOrNull and its lastMutatedAt equals repositoryTransaction.committedAtOrNull. This fences new DeviceRecords, generations, health/owner/reset facts, and current snapshot pointer as one availability change.

For NO_CHANGE, raw capture evidence and candidateDeviceRecords are still retained, while hostSnapshotAfter byte-equals hostSnapshotBeforeOrNull, deviceRecords byte-equals currentDeviceRecordsOrNull, HostAuthority, AvailabilityAuthority, both policy authorities, rollback anchor, commit clock and every repository row remain byte-identical. candidateDeviceRecords may legitimately carry new provenance/timestamps and proposed plus-one coordinates but are not persisted. capturedAt or newly observed raw bytes alone do not force an epoch before either freshness threshold; equal semantics at or beyond a threshold uses REFRESH_COMMITTED, never NO_CHANGE.

Before every decision, snapshotRollbackAuthority.rollbackAuthorityPreflight is a fresh independently root-signed zero-unresolved scan for the exact host/predecessor. Before NO_CHANGE, any reservation already bound to a committed repository candidate must instead be idempotently finalized and freshly read; an unresolved committed epoch cannot be hidden by returning NO_CHANGE. A caller count, absent row in the target repository, or elapsed TTL is not this proof.
x-qmanAtomicCommitRules: A committed mutation set contains exactly one immutable HostSnapshot INSERT, exactly one INSERT for each retained persisted-after deviceRecords artifact, one HostAuthority UPDATE, one global AvailabilityAuthority UPDATE, one ENTITY-HOST-SNAPSHOT-PUBLICATION-AUDIT INSERT, one ENTITY-HOST-SNAPSHOT-PUBLICATION-OUTBOX INSERT and one ENTITY-HOST-SNAPSHOT-PUBLICATION-COMMIT INSERT: exactly deviceRecords length plus six mutations and at most 4102. mutation.x-qmanRecordIdProjection is normative: DeviceRecord uses recordBinding.deviceRecordHash; HostSnapshot contentHash; HostAuthority hostId; AvailabilityAuthority availabilityAuthorityId; audit auditEventId; outbox outboxEventId; commit commitId. Every row count is exact, before/after digests recompute by digestProjection, and no extra mutation exists. V1 publication audit priorAuditDigestOrNull is always null rather than an unverifiable chain label, and the newly inserted pending outbox resourceVersion is exactly 1.

For COMMITTED, repositoryTransaction.commitClockAfter equals commitClockBefore plus exactly one; repositoryCommitRecord carries those byte-equal two clock values and committedAt exact-equals repositoryTransaction.committedAtOrNull. publicationAuditRecord.hostId and publicationOutboxRecord.aggregateId both exact-equal hostSnapshotAfter.state.hostId, and both createdAt values exact-equal repositoryTransaction.committedAtOrNull. Their deterministic event IDs recompute from the exact x-qmanHashRules subject after those equalities hold. For NO_CHANGE, commitClockAfter byte-equals commitClockBefore, commitIdOrNull and committedAtOrNull are null, and no commit, audit or outbox row exists.

The construction order is fixed and acyclic: construct HostSnapshot/DeviceRecord/HostAuthority rows, the availability/audit/outbox projection skeletons, and a repositoryCommitRecord skeleton already carrying transaction/commit/time/recovery keys plus independent HostSnapshot/DeviceRecord/HostAuthority digests; compute the independent outbox payload hash before any mutation projection because its closed preimage contains no mutationSetHash or self-digest, and retain that final payloadHash in the outbox skeleton; compute the commit row's PUBLICATION_COMMIT_DERIVED_FIELDS_NULL afterDigest with exactly mutationSetHash, availabilityAuthorityAfterInstanceSha256, auditRecordInstanceSha256, outboxRecordInstanceSha256 and commitRecordDigest null; compute every other mutation projection, including the outbox projection with its final payloadHash retained; sort and hash the exact N+6 mutation array; insert mutationSetHash into availability/audit/outbox/commit; compute audit/outbox self-digests plus their complete instance hashes; fill the three derived instance hashes in commit, compute commitRecordDigest, and atomically write all rows. Only after repository commit construct visibility probes, finalize/fresh-read the anchor, gate/deliver outbox, then construct traceDigest. A verifier rejects any different null field, domain, order or back-reference.

repositoryCommitRecord is a closed at-commit record and contains only fields declared by its schema from verified request/decision facts, PREPARED rollback-authority facts, the repository transaction and in-transaction row/mutation construction. It must not contain rollbackContextDigest, mutationContextDigest or the mutation receipt contextDigest, resultContextDigest, resultHash, resolvedAuthorityVectorHash, traceDigest, CaseCompletionRecord digest, ExecutionEvidenceIndex digest, or any renamed equivalent derived only after the commit record; those later receipts may point one-way to commitRecordDigest, never back into its preimage. mutationSetHash is the sole permitted mutation-derived set hash in repositoryCommitRecord and remains acyclic only through the declared PUBLICATION_COMMIT_DERIVED_FIELDS_NULL projection.

At least one independently captured BEFORE probe and one independently captured AFTER probe from distinct observerId values are retained. BEFORE exact-projects commitClockBefore, predecessor authority/snapshot/set digests and predecessor commit ID; AFTER exact-projects commitClockAfter, commitId and the complete committed after authority/snapshot/set digests. partialStateObservationCount, orphanHostSnapshotCount, orphanDeviceRecordCount, pointerWithoutCompleteRecordSetCount and availabilityFenceMismatchCount are zero. Readers observe either the complete predecessor or complete successor, never a mixed epoch, pointer, record set or availability fence.

For NO_CHANGE, commitId/committedAt, commit/mutation digests and mutation array are null/empty, every row count is zero, commitClockBefore equals commitClockAfter, and no audit, outbox, last-observed, cache, metric, idempotency or freshness write occurs in the tested product repository.
x-qmanRollbackAndFreshnessRules: Every path first obtains snapshotRollbackAuthority.rollbackAuthorityPreflight as the actual canonical root-signed fresh-nonce zero-unresolved scan for the exact hostId, authorityId and predecessor anchor digest. A committed publication then obtains preparedOrNull as the actual canonical PREPARED external reservation whose prepareReceipt.rollbackAuthorityPreflightReceiptDigest binds that scan, commits the repository transaction while the reservation is valid, and finalizes that exact reservation. prepared/after exact-equal on candidateProjectionDigest and every candidate/CAS field; repository commit, audit and pending outbox exact-equal prepared.prepareReceipt.reservationId, prepareReceipt.receiptDigest, candidateProjectionDigest and required anchorVersion. A failed or rolled-back repository transaction cannot advance the last COMMITTED anchor.

Expiry only forbids a new repository commit. reservationId/candidateProjectionDigest and a non-reusable recovery tombstone remain durably queryable forever. When the retained exact commit row proves repositoryTransaction.committedAtOrNull <= prepareReceipt.expiresAt and binds that reservation, preparation receipt and candidate, publisher startup/reconciler may finalize after expiry and repeated finalize returns the same COMMITTED anchor/receipt without consuming a version. Abort or GC requires independently verifiable repository rollback/non-commit proof for the exact reservation; elapsed TTL alone is insufficient. NO_CHANGE or another reservation on the predecessor is forbidden until every unresolved tombstone is reconciled.

For a non-genesis request, beforeFreshnessOrNull exact-binds beforeOrNull and is live at decoded requestEnvelope.issuedAt; genesis carries both null. For committed paths, captureBatch.captureCompletedAt <= rollbackAuthorityPreflight.state.checkedAt <= prepareReceipt.preparedAt <= freshnessDecision.evaluatedAt = repositoryTransaction.beganAt <= repositoryTransaction.committedAtOrNull <= prepareReceipt.expiresAt, and preflight checkedAt <= preparedAt <= preflight expiresAt. Repository committedAt <= snapshotRollbackAuthority.after.state.updatedAt <= snapshotRollbackAuthority.afterFreshness.state.observedAt <= decoded resultEnvelope.completedAt. Finalization/result may occur after prepare expiresAt because only commit validity is bounded by expiry. For NO_CHANGE, preparedOrNull is null, preflight.checkedAt <= evaluatedAt=beganAt <= preflight.expiresAt, repository has no commit time, and afterFreshness observation occurs at or after beganAt. Every root-signature signedAt lies within its receipt/freshness interval.

snapshotRollbackAuthority.after exact-binds hostSnapshotAfter and hostAuthorityAfter. GENESIS creates anchorVersion/resourceVersion 1; each committed successor or refresh advances both versions by one and binds every predecessor CAS field plus previousAnchorDigestOrNull. INCARNATION_GENESIS starts snapshotEpoch 1 while still advancing the external anchor from the older incarnation. NO_CHANGE has preparedOrNull=null, neither prepares nor advances, and before/after bytes are equal; beforeFreshness and afterFreshness are nevertheless distinct live reads.

afterFreshness.state is a live HOST_SNAPSHOT response for exact after anchor bytes/digest/version/resourceVersion and this trace verifier's fresh nonce. For non-genesis paths the beforeFreshness nonce, rollbackAuthorityPreflight nonce and afterFreshness nonce are pairwise distinct; on committed paths the dispatcher delivery nonce is a fourth distinct value. The stored outbox event remains HOST_SNAPSHOT_PUBLICATION_COMMITTED_PENDING_ANCHOR with zero attempts/successes until finalization. At delivery the dispatcher directly queries the authority using its own fresh nonce retained as outboxDeliveryWitness.deliveryAnchorFreshness; that artifact exact-binds the same COMMITTED anchor and has observedAt <= authorityCheckedAt <= firstDeliveryAttemptAt <= deliveredAt <= expiresAt. The witness exact-binds outbox/recovery keys, is signed by a non-revoked CONTROL_REPOSITORY_EVIDENCE dispatcher key over deliveryReceiptDigest, and proves both pre-anchor counters zero. Only then is HOST_SNAPSHOT_PUBLISHED. Neither the repository pointer nor pending event authorizes planning or host side effects before the separate verifier freshness succeeds.
x-qmanCompletionRules: C00 completion requires this actual same-iteration trace plus raw operation request/result, capture/provider bytes, predecessor and after complete DeviceRecord bytes where applicable, signed snapshots, authority/fence bytes, external PREPARED/COMMITTED anchor/freshness bytes, transaction commit record, audit/outbox and independent zero-partial visibility probes. Decoder declarations, SQL/API logs and aggregate digests do not provide instance coverage.

QMAN_PRODUCT_E3_HOST_SNAPSHOT_PUBLICATION_TRACE requires all four non-null productEvidenceBinding fields to resolve, at the exact raw targetRepositoryCommit, to the active integration mapping core, current C00 Case contract, target build attestation and runner manifest. These are acyclic prior inputs. A later CaseCompletionRecord and ExecutionEvidenceIndex may point one-way to traceDigest and its verified artifact IDs; neither digest may appear in this trace or any trace preimage. Product completion replays every hash, CAS, epoch, projection, completeness, signature, rollback, recovery, freshness and atomicity rule from retained bytes.

REFERENCE_SQLITE_HOST_SNAPSHOT_PUBLICATION_COMPONENT_ONLY and COMPONENT_HOST_SNAPSHOT_PUBLICATION_TRACE_NOT_PRODUCT_CLOSURE can exercise the contract but never close C00, G1, PRODUCT_IMPLEMENTED or QUALIFIED. A fake provider, SQLite/reference adapter, schema-valid synthetic trace, VMware observation, component verifier, or merely setting evidenceBoundary to the product enum remains premise evidence; only the mapped Qman product adapter/build and product repository execution may emit acceptable E3.

Merely setting evidenceBoundary to the product enum is not product proof.
